description: phasekit's machine-readable interface manifest: the environment variables, artifact files and exit codes through which phasekit and any supervisor (an orchestrator, a cron job, a human wrapper) communicate. Hand-authored by the producer; pinned from both directions by tests/test_interface_manifest.py. Refreshing this file is part of acceptance for any change that touches the interface (docs/CONTRACTS.md, 'Producer responsibilities').
standalone_note: Every input here is honoured WHEN SUPPLIED. No supervisor is required: defaults make every script work standalone, and this manifest is equally the contract a stranger's cron job codes against.

scope.covered: scripts/*.sh, scripts/phasekit-contracts.py, and .claude/hooks/*.sh — the shipped runtime surface a supervisor interacts with.
scope.not_covered: Ambient POSIX environment (HOME, PWD, PATH) and the Claude Code harness's own hook payload (HOOK_PAYLOAD via stdin) are not interface knobs and are not declared. install.sh's PHASEKIT_HOME/PHASEKIT_BIN/PHASEKIT_URL/PHASEKIT_REF are the installer's interface, documented in docs/adr/ADR-0002-self-update-channels.md. A supervisor's own artifacts are the supervisor's interface, not phasekit's; their phasekit-side reflection is the env family below (e.g. PHASEKIT_ITERATION_MODE). The one declared exception (v0.14.8) is the `iteration` key of artifacts/iteration-mode.json, which the loop reads into boundary-state.json — everything else in that file stays supervisor-side.

env.name: PHASEKIT_BOUNDARY_KILL_PROBE
env.semantics: Fault injection for the generated kill-point test ONLY (tests/test_boundary_state.py, v0.14.5): '<step>:<pre|post>' SIGKILLs the loop right before (pre) or right after (post) artifacts/boundary-state.json advances to <step> inside land_boundary — a real kill of the shipped code at every seam of the landing sequence. 'gate:footprint' (v0.14.10) SIGKILLs right after the verify gate's command returned and its footprint was measured, before the restore. Never set in production; a supervisor never forwards it.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERIFY_MEMO_TTL_SECONDS
env.semantics: How long (seconds) the verify memo in artifacts/boundary-state.json is honoured (v0.14.5) — a green or red verdict recorded for an exact tree older than this is re-run. The memo cannot see inputs outside the tree (a container image, ignored files, dependencies resolved at build time), so its trust is bounded in time. 0 = never expires.

env.name: PHASEKIT_SESSION_DEADLINE
env.semantics: Epoch seconds of the supervisor's hard kill (the supervisor computes it as start + its MAX_MINUTES); the loop refuses to start an iteration it cannot finish before it and wraps up instead. Non-numeric values are warned about and ignored.

env.name: PHASEKIT_WRAPUP_SENTINEL
env.semantics: Path of the supervisor's soft-stop sentinel file. Existence-only signal: the loop clears a stale one at start, polls between iterations, and finishes with a wrap-up commit when it appears (v0.14.2: when that commit's verify gate is RED but the security pair is untouched and the post-verify gates pass, the loop falls through to the labeled last-resort wip commit instead of leaving a dirty tree — the wip carries the work only: deploy artifacts are disarmed as on the kill path and phase-approval.json stays on disk uncommitted for the stranded-artifact recovery — and prints 'Run wrapped up with UNVERIFIED work committed'); the wrapup-nudge PostToolUse hook additionally surfaces it to the model MID-iteration, once, so a turn spanning the deadline hears about it before the kill. The default lives inside the workspace, so a containerized supervisor signals by writing the file, not by forwarding this variable; an overrider owns keeping a custom path out of git status.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ITERATION_MODE
env.semantics: standard | light. light is the reduced-ceremony loop for small triaged tasks (caps 2/2, no strategy-planner/red-team, escalate-not-grind); it silently downgrades to standard when the verify gate is absent or still the stub.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ITER_RETRY
env.semantics: Per-iteration retry budget for a non-zero claude CLI exit (transient API/CLI failures). 0 disables retries; after the budget is spent the child's exit code propagates verbatim.

env.name: PHASEKIT_PACING_FLOOR_SECONDS
env.semantics: Minimum remaining-time threshold for deadline pacing; no new iteration starts when less than max(this, 1.2 x average pass duration this session, the cost ledger's pass P90) remains before PHASEKIT_SESSION_DEADLINE — the two estimates apply once a pass has completed (a session is never refused its first pass). The one copy of the 180 s default: a supervisor that needs it reads it here. Non-numeric values fall back to the default.

env.name: PHASEKIT_WRAPUP_LEAD_SECONDS
env.default: unset — measured (v0.18.0): L = T_y + M (+ R in light mode), T_y = G_full + W + 60 s, every term the P90 of the cost ledger (artifacts/logs/cost-ledger.json; priors G_full 300 s, G_fast 60 s, W 60 s, M = G_full + 120 s, R = G_full + 300 s on an empty ledger), clamped to [300 s, 25% of the span]; where 25% is under 300 s (a span under 20 minutes) half the span stands in
env.semantics: Seconds before PHASEKIT_SESSION_DEADLINE at which the loop's own deadline watchdog self-arms the wrap-up sentinel (v0.13.0) — the supervisor's touch stays idempotent with it. When set it REPLACES the measured lead verbatim, and the take-control lead is capped by it; 0 disables both self-arming and take-control (supervisor-only). A published knob for standalone use — a supervisor reads the lead in force from the `deadline watchdog: armed` line instead of setting it. Ignored when no deadline is set.

env.name: PHASEKIT_LASTRESORT_LEAD_SECONDS
env.semantics: Seconds before PHASEKIT_SESSION_DEADLINE at which the deadline watchdog makes the last-resort strand commit (v0.13.0): if the tree is dirty it keeps ready-to-deploy.json and project-complete.json OUT of the commit — v0.18.0: unstaged, never rewritten, never deleted (the commit carries HEAD's copies; the session's stay on disk for the next loop start's verify-gated landing; a torn copy is deleted, or restored to HEAD where HEAD tracks it) — refreshes the dead-man baton, and commits --no-verify with transients unstaged and Phasekit-* trailers (Phasekit-Kind: wip). A take-control lead at or inside this one is dropped (the last-resort commit is the next stage anyway). 0 disables. Ignored when no deadline is set.

env.name: PHASEKIT_SQUASH_TARGET
env.semantics: Branch-per-iteration + squash-to-target (v0.14.0). Names the integration branch (e.g. main or master). When set, the loop works on a WORK BRANCH (see PHASEKIT_WORK_BRANCH) and every approval-class commit (phase-approval.json, project-complete.json) is additionally squashed onto this branch as ONE commit whose message is the artifact's suggested_commit_message plus a 'phasekit-squash: <branch>@<sha>' trailer, followed by a merge-back commit on the work branch so the next squash diffs only the next phase. Checkpoints, wrap-up and strand commits stay on the work branch. Nothing is force-pushed. The squash-integrity guard fails closed: if the target's tip (or origin/<target>, best-effort fetch) is not an ancestor of the work branch, the loop writes phase-blocked.json (blocker_kind branch-integrity) and exits 2 with the target untouched. At completion HEAD rests on the target; the work branch is kept. Unset = every commit path behaves as before (byte-identical pin).

env.name: PHASEKIT_WORK_BRANCH
env.semantics: Name of the iteration's work branch under PHASEKIT_SQUASH_TARGET (a supervisor passes e.g. iter/<N>-<slug>). When HEAD is on the target, the loop creates it (or re-enters an existing one that carries nothing the target lacks); when HEAD is already on it, nothing happens; when HEAD is on some other branch the loop blocks rather than guess. Unset with HEAD on the target: the loop creates iter/<UTC stamp>. Ignored when PHASEKIT_SQUASH_TARGET is unset.

env.name: PHASEKIT_FORWARD_ENV
env.semantics: Comma-separated NAMES of project-specific environment keys a supervisor has placed in container-setup.sh's process env (v0.14.3) — the one door for non-PHASEKIT_ keys such as the backend URL a client bakes at build time. container-setup.sh adds `-e NAME` (v0.18.2: by name — the value never on docker's command line; until v0.18.1 `-e NAME=<value>`) for every listed name that is set, skips unset names silently and malformed names loudly, refuses the names the script itself sets for the container (HOME, PATH, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, IS_SANDBOX), forwards the list itself (the loop prints `Project env forwarded by the supervisor: …` at start), and prints a names-only witness (`container: forwarding project env: …`); values never touch a file or a log — a token written as NAME=value is reported by its name part only. Newlines count as separators. Unset: nothing beyond the fixed allowlist crosses the container wall. The Foundry orchestrator sets it from a project's declared env_file (its #562). v0.16.2: `phasekit upgrade` (scripts/enrich-project.py) forwards the same keys by name to its container gate, refusing HOME, PATH, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, IS_SANDBOX, PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_DIR, GIT_USER_NAME and GIT_USER_EMAIL; the gate's own git config and session values follow them, so a forwarded key never overrides them. v0.18.2: each listed key crosses as `-e NAME` (docker reads the value from its own environment) — until v0.18.1 it was `-e NAME=value`, which put the value on docker's command line, readable by every account on the host in the process table.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CMD
env.default: unset — the loop runs scripts/phasekit-verify.sh if present
env.semantics: One-shot shell command overriding the project's verify gate; run via bash -eo pipefail -c. Non-empty also satisfies light-mode verify eligibility on its own. v0.16.0: also the gate `phasekit upgrade` runs on the upgraded tree before committing, under the same bash -eo pipefail -c.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERIFY_BUDGET_SECONDS
env.semantics: STANDALONE only since v0.18.0 (no PHASEKIT_SESSION_DEADLINE): seconds above which one verify run counts as over budget; after two such runs the loop prints a one-time fail-open advisory suggesting a fast tier. Under a session bound the advisory is measured instead — once per session when the full tier's P90 in the cost ledger exceeds 12.5% of the bound. Non-numeric values fall back to the default.

env.name: VERIFY_SKIP
env.semantics: 1 bypasses the pre-commit verify gate for a run (the routine hatch for red-TDD commits and docs-only phases) and clears artifacts/phase-verify-failed.json. Deliberately does NOT bypass the contracts gate. Also honoured by the seeded scripts/phasekit-verify.sh templates.

env.name: VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS
env.semantics: Consecutive verify-failure circuit breaker; on reaching it the loop writes artifacts/phase-blocked.json (standard) or escalates via artifacts/light-escalation.json (light) and stops with exit 2.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_SKIP
env.default: unset — contracts gate runs when contracts.yaml declares dependencies
env.semantics: 1 is the loud, operator-only, one-run bypass of the cross-project contracts gate (docs/CONTRACTS.md). Never a committed setting; checked before the missing-checker refusal so it also wins there.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_MOUNT
env.default: unset — no contracts provider (the normal standalone case)
env.semantics: HOST path to a provider's contracts tree (index.json + one directory per slug). Bind-mounted read-only at /contracts inside the container, announced inward as PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_DIR=/contracts. Set-but-unusable (not a directory, or no readable index.json) is a hard exit 1, never a silent drop. v0.16.2: `phasekit upgrade` mounts the same tree the same way for its gate (a set-but-unusable one refuses the upgrade, exit 4); the host-mode gate sees it as PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_DIR.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_DIR
env.semantics: Where the provider's contracts tree is readable, consumed by the contracts checker. Set by container-setup.sh when PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_MOUNT is given; a standalone user sets it by hand to run the gate outside a container. v0.16.2: when set on the upgrading host (and PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_MOUNT is not), `phasekit upgrade` bind-mounts it read-only at /contracts for its container gate and sets this to /contracts there; never forwarded by PHASEKIT_FORWARD_ENV.

env.name: PHASEKIT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK
env.semantics: 1 skips the once-per-run, non-fatal upstream release-tag nudge (git ls-remote against the manifest's origin_url).

env.name: PHASEKIT_TRACE
env.semantics: 1 enables bash set -x in the wrapper scripts; container-setup.sh forwards any non-empty value into the container so in-container scripts trace too.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTAINER_NAME
env.default: unset — docker assigns a random name
env.semantics: Deterministic docker --name so an outer supervisor can docker kill the container on session timeout.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CONTAINER_USER
env.semantics: Raw docker run --user spec; root normalizes to 0:0 (with HOME=/home/node pinned and IS_SANDBOX=1 exported). Takes precedence over PHASEKIT_ROOTLESS_DOCKER. v0.16.0: also the user `phasekit upgrade` runs the project's gate as in the runner image.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ROOTLESS_DOCKER
env.semantics: 1 (with PHASEKIT_CONTAINER_USER empty) runs the container as root, the UID-0 mode for rootless Docker where container root maps to the unprivileged host user. v0.16.0: also decides the user the upgrade gate runs as in the runner image (0:0 when rootless, the host uid otherwise; detected from the daemon when unset).

env.name: PHASEKIT_PYTHON
env.semantics: Interpreter used to run scripts/enrich-project.py, so a global install can point at an isolated venv (e.g. one that has pyyaml).

env.name: PHASEKIT_UPGRADE_VERIFY
env.semantics: v0.16.0. Where `phasekit upgrade` runs the project's own gate on the upgraded tree before committing: auto = the runner image when docker is reachable, the host only when there is no docker CLI at all (a daemon that fails or hangs, or a missing image, is a refusal, never a silent host run); container = the runner image or nothing; host = the host; off = no gate. --no-verify and --no-commit also mean off. A project whose gate was not configured before the upgrade (no scripts/phasekit-verify.sh, or still the stub) is skipped. Anything but a clean green (red, timed out, a footprint in the tree, or unable to run) restores every file the upgrade wrote byte-for-byte, commits nothing and exits 4. Any other value is an error (exit 1).

env.name: PHASEKIT_UPGRADE_VERIFY_TIMEOUT
env.semantics: v0.16.0. Seconds the upgrade gate may run before it is treated as red (tree restored, nothing committed). A non-integer falls back to the default.

env.name: PHASEKIT_RUNNER_IMAGE
env.semantics: v0.16.0. The runner image the upgrade gate uses in auto and container modes; the project is mounted read-write at /workspace with git safe.directory set. v0.16.2: a session's environment — HOME=/home/node for uid 0 or 1000 (a throwaway HOME otherwise), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, IS_SANDBOX=1 as root, a global git identity (GIT_USER_NAME/GIT_USER_EMAIL, else the repo's, else 'phasekit upgrade'), and the contracts provider read-only at /contracts.

env.name: CLAUDE_MODE
env.semantics: new = fresh session (also resets a stale phase-verify-failed.json at kickoff); continue = resume the most recent session (-c). The loop consumes it for iteration 1 and sets it per child invocation thereafter.

env.name: MAX_ITERATIONS
env.semantics: Loop iteration ceiling; exhausting it without completion is exit 3. container-setup.sh forwards it only when set, deliberately leaving the mode-aware default to the loop.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_MODEL
env.semantics: Model for the claude invocation (alias like sonnet or a full claude-* id), passed as --model when non-empty. The light-mode final review deliberately unsets it so the review runs on the default model; the value is also recorded in light-escalation.json.

env.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
env.default: unset — fall back to volume-persisted subscription credentials
env.semantics: Pay-per-token API key, forwarded into the container only when non-empty. Missing both this and volume credentials is a warning, not an error.

env.name: AUTO_PUSH
env.semantics: 1 makes the loop git push after every loop-created commit (iteration and wrap-up); push failure is non-fatal.

env.name: IMAGE_NAME
env.semantics: Docker image tag to build/run.

env.name: CLAUDE_VOLUME
env.semantics: Named Docker volume mounted at /home/node/.claude, holding persisted Claude subscription credentials — one volume is the fleet's shared auth.

env.name: PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION
env.semantics: Passed as --build-arg at image build time (not a runtime -e).

env.name: SKIP_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP
env.semantics: Non-empty skips Playwright MCP injection by the container entrypoint.

env.name: GIT_USER_NAME
env.semantics: Git author name inside the container. v0.16.2: also the upgrade gate's global identity when set.

env.name: GIT_USER_EMAIL
env.semantics: Git author email inside the container. v0.16.2: also the upgrade gate's global identity when set.

env.name: GH_TOKEN
env.semantics: GitHub token for HTTPS push / gh CLI, forwarded when set. GITHUB_TOKEN is honoured independently under its own name.

env.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
env.semantics: Alternate name for GH_TOKEN; both are forwarded independently when set.

env.name: SSH_AUTH_SOCK
env.default: unset or not a socket — no agent forwarding
env.semantics: Host ssh-agent socket, bind-mounted into the container and rewritten to /ssh-agent for the child.

env.name: CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT
env.default: empty — the hook reads its payload from stdin; with neither, it allows
env.semantics: A FALLBACK since v0.18.2: the Claude Code harness gives a PreToolUse hook its payload as JSON on stdin ({tool_input: {command}, cwd, …} — probed in scaffold-runner, claude 2.1.285) and never sets this variable, so until v0.18.1 the hook matched nothing. The hook reads stdin first and this variable only when stdin is empty (an older harness, a hand test).

env.name: PHASEKIT_STOP_BLOCK_LIMIT
env.semantics: Max Stop-hook blocks per iteration before the require-verdict hook steps aside and lets the loop's own no-verdict handling take over. Non-numeric values fall back to the default.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERDICT_ARTIFACTS
env.semantics: Space-separated verdict-artifact vocabulary, exported by the loop from its VERDICT_ARTIFACTS array (the single source of truth) so the Stop hook and the dispatcher cannot disagree about what an ending is. Not honoured from the outer environment: the loop assigns it unconditionally.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ARTIFACTS_DIR
env.semantics: Absolute path of the repo's artifacts/ directory, exported by the loop for the Stop hook. Not honoured from the outer environment: the loop assigns it unconditionally.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ITER_MARKER
env.semantics: Path of the loop's iteration-start marker file (a mktemp path, touched before every claude invocation); the Stop hook only counts verdict artifacts newer than it.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ENV_KEY
env.default: a random per-session value the loop generates and exports before any turn
env.semantics: v0.18.0, internal: the key of the loop's hashed environment snapshot (artifacts/logs/.loop-env, names and keyed value hashes, never values), which a model's `phasekit verify` compares its own environment with before its verdict may be reused by the commit gate. Never set it; never forward it.

env.name: PHASEKIT_ITER
env.semantics: Iteration number embedded in the per-iteration log filenames (artifacts/logs/claude-iter-N.*). Set per invocation by the loop; the manual default labels direct run-phase.sh runs.

env.name: PHASEKIT_RETRY_ATTEMPT
env.semantics: Retry ordinal for the current iteration; >0 appends -retryN to log filenames so a retry never overwrites the first attempt's logs.

env.name: IS_SANDBOX
env.semantics: Set to 1 for the container only when running as UID 0, because Claude Code refuses --permission-mode bypassPermissions as root without it.

env.name: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
env.semantics: Unconditionally set for the container so the claude CLI finds the volume-persisted credentials regardless of the effective user.

env.name: PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CONFIGURED
env.semantics: NOT read from the environment: a sentinel LINE inside the project-owned scripts/phasekit-verify.sh. The seeded stub carries PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CONFIGURED=0; a configured gate flips it to 1. The loop greps for it to decide light-mode eligibility, and enrich-project.py uses it to know the stub may be replaced by a stack template on upgrade.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CHANNEL_DEFAULT
env.semantics: Library constant (unconditional assignment when sourced), not an input knob: the channel used when a scaffold checkout has no .phasekit-channel file. Setting it in the environment has no effect.

env.name: PHASEKIT_CANONICAL_ORIGIN
env.semantics: Internal constant: the fallback upstream URL for the release-tag nudge when the manifest carries no origin_url. Setting it in the environment has no effect.

env.name: PHASEKIT_LEARNINGS_WARN_KB
env.semantics: Advisory-only threshold in KB for the once-per-session docs/LEARNINGS.md size note. At or over the threshold the loop prints one stderr line suggesting a curation pass per the file's own header rule; it never blocks, never rotates, and never alters prompts (the doc-rotation descope, 2026-08-20). Non-numeric values disable the check. Supervisors that want scheduling watch the same file size themselves.

artifacts.name: phase-approval.json
artifacts.lifecycle: durable — committed with the phase, deliberately never deleted by iteration cleanup; v0.18.0: stamped by the loop at landing like project-complete.json (`iteration` written or corrected, `base`); its `deferrals` (entries opened) and `closes` (keys closed) are applied to artifacts/deferrals.json but the approval itself keeps them as written; its landing writes the phase-close evidence artifacts/iterations/<N>/<phase>.json into the same commit; a refused landing leaves it unstaged, never staged; v0.18.2: its landing stamps `plan_paths` (see the planned-paths convention) — the phase's changed paths against the `Planned paths:` its docs/PHASES.md section declares
artifacts.when: Written by the Claude session at the end of a phase to approve it; the loop commits it (freshness-gated against the iteration-start marker). v0.14.5: an optional 'final_phase': true names it the project's last approval — the loop then records artifacts/project-complete.json itself (derived: summary + deferrals carried, provenance named) when the session has not written one, so 'approved but unrecorded' cannot survive a kill. Every 'deferrals' entry is committed with a stable 'key' (explicit, else the cited AC#n, else a slug of the item's first words — never a hash); an entry the loop cannot key (no key, no AC number, no ASCII words in the item) stays keyless with a WARN — it stays in its record as written but cannot enter the v0.18.0 deferral ledger. v0.14.7: an optional 'iteration' (the fleet convention: the string 'iteration-<N>' the supervisor's change request names) is carried into the project-complete.json the loop synthesizes from a final approval. v0.18.0: the loop STAMPS 'iteration' from the supervisor's artifacts/iteration-mode.json — written when absent, corrected when the record names another iteration (never in a standalone run, where the approval's own value stands).

artifacts.name: phase-update.json
artifacts.lifecycle: committed when produced, deleted at each iteration start
artifacts.when: Written by the session when it revised the phase plan/roadmap instead of approving a phase; the loop commits it.

artifacts.name: project-complete.json
artifacts.lifecycle: durable — committed as the project's completion record; deleted at each iteration start until real (v0.18.2: except THIS boundary's committed completion while it is still landing — the commit that landed the record comes after this iteration's base (the supervisor's intake, else the recorded work base), and the record's boundary — the current one, or the one archived as `previous` when a new pass began before its walk — is this iteration's (same supervisor label, else same work branch) and either `unlanded` names its commit or the boundary is final and stopped at step 1..5; the next loop start resumes such a landing before any turn — which a new pass, a carry nobody re-claimed and a synthesized record that did not land never delete: they restore its committed bytes, because a deletion on disk is what the next checkpoint commits, un-recording the completion; an EARLIER completion HEAD still carries — a project resumed for new work — goes as before, and a deletion already on disk, a human's or an intake's, is left). v0.14.5: the loop itself writes it (recorded_by names the step) when the landed approval carries final_phase: true and the session left none. v0.14.7: that synthesized record carries 'iteration' verbatim from the approval (null when the approval names none — the key is always present), so a supervisor can resolve which iteration it closes; and the deadline watchdog's last-resort commit never deletes a session-authored copy HEAD does not carry — it stays on disk, uncommitted, for the next loop start's verify-gated landing — kept only when it parses as a JSON object (a torn file from an interrupted writer is deleted as before); an untracked ready-to-deploy.json is still deleted: a deploy claim no landing step owns. v0.18.0: the loop STAMPS it at landing (never refusing — fork F5): `iteration` (the supervisor's, written when absent and corrected when the record names another), `base` (the commit the iteration started from), `final_phase` (this iteration's approval phase, when absent) and `recorded_by` (when absent); its `deferrals` are COMPOSED — the session lists only the entries it opened (`deferrals`) and the keys it closed (`closes`), the loop applies both to artifacts/deferrals.json and writes the full open set back here, so a reader sees the same set copy-forward produced. A completion whose landing is REFUSED (red gate, a refusing commit gate) is carried: unstaged, kept on disk (`??` or ` M`, never `AD`), claiming nothing until the session re-writes it; the next iteration's cleanup leaves it for the repair turn to edit. v0.18.1: a commit made DURING a model turn that lands it (the model ran `git commit` itself) ends that turn — the completion is terminal, the model gets no further tool call in it — and the light review, which precedes the final commit, does not run over it; anything written after the commit that landed it is restored at the rest and named (boundary-state.json `post_completion`). v0.18.2 (the loop owns every commit): the command guard refuses a model's git writes under the loop, and whoever committed this record, the walk's step 3 is proven only on a CLEAN tree — work the committing commit did not carry lands through the loop's own verify-gated completion commit (subject from the plan, body naming the commit it completes), or, when the gate refuses it, stays in the tree, is named (boundary-state.json `unlanded`, stderr) and the walk stops at step 3 like any red completion; a completion commit the loop lands directly also stamps `plan_paths`. v0.18.5: every loop write of the record (the landing stamp, deferral-key normalization, the composed `deferrals`, `plan_paths`, the step-3 synthesis) writes its keys in ONE order — `iteration` first, then the other scalar keys, then the arrays and objects — so a reader of the file's prefix finds every scalar at once however large `deferrals` grows (xmeo, 2026-10-01: a 382 KB record with `iteration` after a ~218 KB `deferrals` stalled a 256 KB prefix reader ~9 h); key names, values and the order inside each value are unchanged
artifacts.when: Written by the session when every phase is approved and acceptance criteria are met; in light mode it must survive an adversarial final review to count. Its presence after the final commit is the loop's exit-0 signal.

artifacts.name: phase-blocked.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — deleted at each iteration start; kept out of commits but deliberately visible in git status
artifacts.when: Written by the session when it needs external input, or by the loop itself when VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS consecutive verify failures trip the circuit breaker, or (v0.14.0, blocker_kind branch-integrity) when branch-per-iteration cannot proceed: the squash target moved out-of-band, HEAD is detached / on an unexpected branch, or the target branch is missing; or (v0.18.2, blocker_kind landing) when a FINAL boundary's worktree still differs from HEAD, at the squash or plain step 4, in paths no loop commit can carry (the loop never judges a tree it does not land) — named in `reason`, rather than re-entering to MAX_ITERATIONS. Either way the loop stops with exit 2.

artifacts.name: phase-verify-failed.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — cleared on verify pass, on VERIFY_SKIP, or at a fresh CLAUDE_MODE=new kickoff; NOT a verdict (the session is still expected to answer); visible in git status
artifacts.when: Written by the loop after each failed verify (or contracts-gate) run, carrying the failure for the next iteration to fix. attempts feeds the circuit breaker. v0.18.2: also written for a refusal of a commit a turn's verdict drives (commit_from_artifact) or of the kept-out claim's landing that is not the gate — the credential scan of docs/LEARNINGS*.md (label `commit gate (after verify)`; only the REFUSED line, never the matched text), a path git cannot stage (`git add (paths git cannot stage)`, the paths named), git refusing the commit (`git commit …`, git's stderr) — with `commit_refusal: true`: a green gate does not clear it (its attempts count to the breaker), a commit that happens does. v0.14.10: a gate that WROTE to the tree is red even when its command exited 0 (exit_code stays the command's own; null when the command never returned — a footprint settled at loop start after a kill inside the gate, attempts unchanged): gate_footprint lists the paths the loop restored (tracked, back to HEAD) or deleted (untracked), gate_footprint_rule is the verify-gate-read-only convention's sentence and gate_footprint_recipe the fix (gate output under artifacts/logs/ or another ignored path); the three keys are absent on an ordinary red. Dirt present before the gate is the session's and never appears here.

artifacts.name: session-handoff.json
artifacts.lifecycle: durable across the boundary — committed with the wrap-up; the NEXT session's continue prompt reads then deletes it
artifacts.when: Written by the loop on wrap-up paths (sentinel honoured or deadline pacing) as the baton for the next session.

artifacts.name: ready-to-deploy.json
artifacts.lifecycle: durable — committed inside the iteration's work; v0.18.0: never rewritten or deleted by an UNVERIFIED commit path (the watchdog's last-resort commit, the wrap-up fall-through, the gate-pending index commit) — it is unstaged, so the wip carries HEAD's copy and the worktree keeps the session's, which the next verify-gated landing stages with the rest of its coherent tree (a torn copy is deleted, or restored to HEAD where HEAD tracks it). A claim HEAD does not carry byte-for-byte is not a verified claim; a supervisor publishes only one HEAD carries
artifacts.when: Written by the session when the project is ready for a deploy; phasekit's scripts neither read nor write it — the vocabulary is defined by phasekit's workflow docs (docs/QUALITY_GATES.md) and the file is the supervisor's deploy trigger.

artifacts.name: scope-refusal.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — hidden from git status; consumed from disk by the supervisor
artifacts.when: Written by the loop's commit gate when a light-mode iteration staged scaffold-class files it may not touch; the commit is refused and light mode escalates (exit 2).

artifacts.name: light-escalation.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — hidden from git status; consumed from disk by the supervisor
artifacts.when: Written by the loop when a light-mode run needs promotion to a standard iteration (scope refusal, repeated verify failure, review withdrawal, or the iteration cap). Accompanies exit 2 (or exit 3 for the cap).

artifacts.name: scope-warning.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — hidden from git status; advisory only
artifacts.when: Written by the loop's commit gate when a standard-mode commit touches scaffold-class files — allowed, but flagged for the operator.

artifacts.name: spec-change.json
artifacts.lifecycle: transient signal — hidden from git status; read-then-deleted by the supervisor
artifacts.when: Written by the loop's commit gate when docs/SPEC.md is part of the staged change, so a supervisor can surface spec drift.

artifacts.name: wrapup-requested
artifacts.lifecycle: sentinel — existence-only, contents never read; cleared stale at loop start, removed once honoured; excluded from git status
artifacts.when: Written by the outer supervisor at T-minus-N to request a soft stop; the loop finishes the current iteration, wrap-up commits, and exits 0.

artifacts.name: mutation-run.json
artifacts.lifecycle: audit record of an opt-in mutation-testing run (with-mutation profile only)
artifacts.when: Written by the opt-in mutation harness when a session runs the mutation protocol; see docs/MUTATION_TESTING.md.

artifacts.name: logs
artifacts.lifecycle: internal — never committed (the loop unstages artifacts/logs on every commit path) and excluded from git status
artifacts.when: claude-iter-N[-retryM].jsonl (raw stream-json + stderr) and .log (rendered via phasekit-log-fmt.sh) per claude invocation. v0.18.0: also cost-ledger.json (the per-project cost model: the last 20 samples per measure — g_full, g_fast, w, m, r, pass — and the last 20 sessions with bound, lead, take-control, at_cap, heavy, exit yielded|took-control|killed; persists across sessions, read by the loop only — a supervisor reads the `phasekit-cost:` line), .deadline-yield (written when the watchdog takes control of a turn; the loop reads it; cleared at loop start), .loop-env (the loop's environment as names and truncated value hashes, never values, for `phasekit verify`'s reuse check; removed at exit), .carried-completion (the carry marker of a completion record whose landing was refused; v0.18.1: its content is the carried record's blob, so a commit that sweeps it in unchanged claims nothing), claude.pid ("<pid> <role>" of the model turn in flight, written by run-phase.sh and removed when the turn ends — the deadline watchdog's take-control target), v0.18.1: .completion-yield (written when the completion turn guard saw a commit land artifacts/project-complete.json during a turn on a clean tree and ended that turn; the loop reads it; cleared at loop start), .completion-guard-start (touched when a turn's guard starts; the freshness reference for .completion-yield), completion-guard.log (the guard's own log, one per project), post-completion/<stamp>/ (the bytes of paths written after the completion commit that the loop restored: tracked.patch and untracked/ — never committed), the per-subagent nudge markers and repeat clocks (.wrapup-nudge-*), and lock/tmp files of the loop's records.

artifacts.name: .scope-check.tmp
artifacts.lifecycle: internal staging file for the scope check; promoted to scope-warning.json or removed within one gate run; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: Exists only inside post_verify_commit_gates. Do not rely on it.

artifacts.name: .wrapup-nudge-sent
artifacts.lifecycle: internal marker (empty file) of the MAIN agent's first wrap-up nudge this iteration — its mtime is when the nudge was delivered (the cost model's M); v0.18.0: a subagent's marker is artifacts/logs/.wrapup-nudge-sent.<agent_id> (the harness names subagents in the hook payload), so a subagent never spends the main agent's nudge; freshness against the iteration marker decides, and iteration cleanup deletes them all beside .stop-hook-blocks; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: The wrapup-nudge hook's per-agent, once-per-iteration bookkeeping (PreToolUse refuses once per agent; PostToolUse repeats at most once per 60 s per agent). Do not rely on it.

artifacts.name: .wrapup-in-progress
artifacts.lifecycle: internal session-end marker (empty file, v0.13.1): touched at wrapup_commit entry so the deadline watchdog's last-resort phase stands down instead of racing the gated wrap-up; never removed on the wrap-up path (every wrap-up exit ends the session) and deleted at each iteration start beside the nudge marker; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: Mutual exclusion between the loop's two session-end committers. Do not rely on it.

artifacts.name: session-interrupted.json
artifacts.lifecycle: dead-man baton: written at every iteration start, deleted by the loop's EXIT trap when the iteration concludes with a verdict; one that survives to the NEXT session's start is promoted to session-handoff.json (unless a real wrap-up baton exists, which wins) and consumed by the orientation there. Same six keys as session-handoff.json. Never committed; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: The previous session was killed or exited without concluding its iteration. Read via its promotion to session-handoff.json, not directly.

artifacts.name: .stop-hook-blocks
artifacts.lifecycle: internal per-iteration counter (plain integer, not JSON); deleted by iteration cleanup so the block budget resets; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: The Stop hook's bounded-block bookkeeping. Do not rely on it.

artifacts.name: iteration-mode.json
artifacts.lifecycle: supervisor-owned and COMMITTED by the supervisor (the orchestrator writes it inside the iteration commit); optional — absent in a standalone run. phasekit never writes or deletes it; the loop reads ONE key at each pass start (v0.14.8)
artifacts.when: The supervising iteration's label. boundary_begin copies `iteration` verbatim into boundary-state.json's `iteration` when it is a number or a string (never normalised, never derived from the work-branch name); a missing file, an unparseable file, a record without the key, or any other value type (object, array, boolean, null) reads as null. A consumer that requires an int MUST treat any other carried value as 'no label' (null), never as a corrupt record. The file's other keys (mode, grade, rationale, task_id, …) are the supervisor's own and are not read by phasekit — the execution mode still arrives as PHASEKIT_ITERATION_MODE.

artifacts.name: deferrals.json
artifacts.lifecycle: v0.18.0: the OPEN deferrals, committed and tool-maintained (the changesets shape): at every approval-class landing the loop upserts the record's `deferrals` by key and removes its `closes` keys, and writes the full open set into the committed completion record. Seeded once from the last committed completion record. Never hand-edited; deterministic (no clock)
artifacts.when: Present once a v0.18.0 loop has landed an approval-class record. A supervisor may read `open` directly; the completion record's `deferrals` carry the same set.

artifacts.name: iterations
artifacts.lifecycle: v0.18.0: phase-close EVIDENCE, committed inside the landing it describes: at every approval landing of a supervised iteration the loop writes artifacts/iterations/<N>/<phase>.json (complete.json for a completion commit) — {schema, iteration, phase, base, since, changed: [{path, status, sha256}], note}, `changed` being what the phase changed since `since` (the target tip in branch-per-iteration, else the iteration's previous phase/completion commit, else the base) with the sha256 of each staged file. A test reads it instead of git history. The directory's top level is the supervisor's (Foundry archives `pre-iteration-<N>-project-complete.json` there); phasekit writes only the <N>/ subdirectories. v0.18.2: the file also carries `plan_paths` (the planned-paths convention), the same object the landed record carries
artifacts.when: Written by the loop, never by a session; supervised iterations only (a standalone run has no iteration to file it under).

artifacts.name: scratch
artifacts.lifecycle: v0.18.2: the session's sanctioned scratch space — ignored (.git/info/exclude, and unstaged by every commit path should a project .gitignore re-include it), never committed, cleared when an iteration starts (a new supervising iteration label in artifacts/iteration-mode.json, or every session start when no supervisor names one); a second session of the same iteration keeps it
artifacts.when: Anything a session writes that is not the iteration's work (notes, probes, downloaded fixtures) goes here or under /tmp — the loop commits everything else it finds in the tree (`git add -A`), and phasekit cannot tell scratch from work anywhere else.

artifacts.name: boundary-state.json
artifacts.lifecycle: the ONE record of the landing sequence (v0.14.5; schema 2 since v0.14.8): reset to step 0 at every pass start, advanced only by the loop's land_boundary as each step is PROVEN from git/disk (0 idle, 1 approved, 2 committed, 3 recorded, 4 squashed, 5 merged-back, 6 armed, 7 rested); survives across sessions so the next loop start continues an unfinished boundary before any model turn. v0.14.9: a final boundary whose completion has landed (final true at step >= 6) is the iteration's TERMINAL state — the session exits 0 at rest and nothing else runs (no next pass, no wrap-up/pacing or watchdog commit, no phase-blocked.json, no baton); a session that begins on an iteration the record already shows complete (same supervisor label, else same work branch, completion record still landed) exits at once with zero model turns; step 7 unproven only by a tree the verify gate dirtied after the completion commit is named and left uncommitted (a supervisor's clean-tree deploy gate then defers; the fix is the project's gate), never re-entered. v0.18.1: a write made AFTER the completion commit (a model turn that went on after committing the record itself, a process it left running, a hand between sessions) no longer leaves step 7 unproven — the walk restores it (when the loop holds a snapshot of that commit — the guard's or its own) at the walk's start, at step 3 and again before the rest is proven, names it (`post_completion`, stderr) and keeps its bytes under artifacts/logs/post-completion/ (a path whose bytes cannot be kept is not restored); what can still leave step 7 unproven is dirt OLDER than the completion commit that the commit did not carry, named and left as is. Never committed; hidden from git status
artifacts.when: A supervisor READS it instead of inferring 'done' from file presence and mtimes: step 7 with final true = the project's completion landed and HEAD rests; step 7 with final false = a phase boundary landed; step < 7 = the previous session ended mid-sequence (killed_after names the step the deadline watchdog observed at the kill, killed_mode 'kill' or 'wrapup'). sha_at_step maps '2','3','5','7' to the work-branch commit and '4' to the target tip that proved the step; verify_memo is the last GREEN gate {tree_sha (git write-tree), tier fast|full, label, command, passed_at} the loop reuses for the same tree; deploy records whether ready-to-deploy.json was present (and its mtime) when the boundary armed — the mtime rule stays the supervisor's; previous is the boundary that ended before the current idle record began (its final step, phase, final flag and shas), so 'what last landed' survives the next pass's reset. Steps 4-5 are proven trivially without PHASEKIT_SQUASH_TARGET. v0.14.8 (schema 2): `pass` is this session's index inside the MAX_ITERATIONS loop (1, 2, …; 0 when loop-start recovery opened the record before the first pass); `iteration` is the SUPERVISING iteration's label (number or string) copied verbatim from artifacts/iteration-mode.json's `iteration` when the supervisor declared one, else null — phasekit never derives it from the branch name. A schema-1 record (v0.14.5–v0.14.7) has no `pass`, and its `iteration` IS the pass counter (every live record read 1): a consumer distinguishes the two by `schema` and, for schema 1, derives the iteration from `branch` instead. `previous` carries the archived boundary's own keys INCLUDING its `schema` — a schema-1 boundary a v0.14.7 session left is archived as it was, and stays there (a new pass replaces `previous` only when the boundary it ends advanced past step 0), so a schema-1 `previous` can sit under a schema-2 record until the next boundary lands. A consumer branches on the `schema` of the block it reads (top-level or `previous`), never on the top-level value alone. v0.14.10: `verify_red` also carries `gate_footprint` (the paths, or null) so a red-by-footprint replays as the same red; `gate_pending` {before: [base64 of each `git status --porcelain` record ('XY<TAB>path', raw bytes) taken before the gate command], command, label, at} exists only while a verify gate command is running or its footprint is not yet restored — a record found with it at loop start means the previous session died inside its gate, and the loop settles that footprint (restore + red) before any turn, then removes the key. A supervisor never acts on it. v0.18.0: `work_base` {branch, sha} is the target tip the loop created the work branch from — the iteration base when no supervisor names an iteration. v0.18.1 (writes after the completion commit): `completion_snapshot` {blob, commit, source (turn-guard | landing), at, before} is the tree at a final boundary's completion commit, taken only when the loop OBSERVED that state — the turn guard when it saw the completion committed with the tree clean, the walk right after its own completion-carrying commit: `blob` the committed record's blob, `commit` the commit that landed it, `before` the base64 'XY<TAB>path' records of the dirt present then — never judged by a file's time; it covers the window until the loop next dispatches a model turn and is removed then (a dispatched turn is never residue); `post_completion` {restored, residue, commit, at} names every path written AFTER that commit that the loop restored (tracked: to the committed bytes; untracked: removed) at step 3 and at the rest, and `residue` the directory under artifacts/logs/post-completion/ that keeps their bytes (tracked.patch, untracked/). Present only when something was restored; a supervisor may surface it, never acts on it — the tree already rests. v0.18.2: `plan_paths` is the last approval-class landing's plan check (the planned-paths convention; the same object the landed record carries). `unlanded` {paths, reason, completion_commit, at} exists when a final boundary's completion record was committed but the rest of the tree could not be landed through the loop's verify-gated commit (a red gate, a refusing commit gate): the paths stay in the tree, the walk stopped at step 3, and the next turn repairs them; carried across passes and removed once the rest lands (or the final boundary rests). While it names the commit that landed the record, the pass-start cleanup KEEPS the committed record on disk (it still claims, so the repair turn's end lands the rest). Content inside a submodule is never counted as the tree's dirt (`git status --ignore-submodules=dirty`), and neither is an in-tree custom wrap-up sentinel. Plain mode (no squash target) proves step 4 as 'HEAD's tree passed the verify gate' — the loop's green verify_memo for exactly HEAD's tree, else the gate run by the step's action on a tree that IS HEAD's; in branch-per-iteration mode the catch-up squash likewise judges only a worktree that equals HEAD's tree (a difference waits for the next verify-gated commit).

conventions.name: spec-acceptance-criteria-append-only
conventions.semantics: The SPEC's acceptance-criteria section is append-only: sessions add criteria and supersede them (prefix the old line with the marker, exactly, followed by the replacement criterion's number and a colon-space; full replacement text lives in the appended criterion), and never delete or renumber. Removals only via operator change-request. The marker literal is the cross-repo contract a supervisor's spec-change detector keys on: a removal or rewrite of an existing criterion line without it is a high-confidence violation; append-only changes auto-clear.

conventions.name: approval-deferrals
conventions.semantics: Verdict artifacts (phase-approval.json, project-complete.json) may carry a top-level 'deferrals' array of {item, reason, suggested_task} objects plus an optional 'key', one entry per in-scope acceptance item the session deliberately did not implement. 'item' MUST name the AC number when the deferral maps to a criterion. 'key' is the stable dedupe identifier: it defaults to that AC number (e.g. 'AC#3') when 'item' cites one, and MUST be supplied explicitly (kebab-case) otherwise; entries with the same key across artifact rewrites or successive approvals are the SAME deferral and are never refiled. v0.14.5: the loop writes the key into the committed artifact itself (explicit, else AC#n, else a slug of the item's first words; a derived one carries key_derived: ac|slug), so a supervisor never mints a hash; an entry the loop cannot key (no key, no AC number, no ASCII words in the item) stays keyless with a WARN — kept in its own record, never in the v0.18.0 deferral ledger. The supervisor files one queue task per new key so deferred scope cannot lose its slot — and those tasks land HELD (ops lane or approval-gated), never pre-approved: a session's own deferral entry is not self-granted authorization for follow-up work. Absence of the field claims everything in scope shipped; a deferral recorded only in prose is a violation of the deferred-scope gate — this field is the sole machine-readable home. v0.14.12 — severity: Each entry may carry `severity`, one of exactly `BLOCKER | MAJOR | MINOR`. Any other word is not a grade: a consumer treats it as absent and files nothing for it; the session that wrote it has recorded no grade. Absent means MINOR; an explicit null is read as absent (the loop is silent on it; a consumer may warn once and grades it MINOR — no row is lost either way). Matching is case-insensitive with surrounding whitespace ignored (`major` and ` MAJOR ` are MAJOR; the canonical spelling is upper-case). The loop WARNs once per artifact naming the key and the word and never rewrites a session's grade (no red); the sibling key severity_enum is the machine-readable form a supervisor pins against, in filing order (BLOCKER and MAJOR file a queue row; MINOR stays in the ledger — the supervisor's floor, not phasekit's).

conventions.name: blocked-reason-review-nonconvergence
conventions.semantics: The exact 'reason' literal a session writes into artifacts/phase-blocked.json when the review-fix convergence gate trips (two consecutive fix rounds each introduced new MAJOR findings). Sessions must use the literal verbatim; a supervisor branching on blocked-reason may key on it to route non-convergence to an operator or redesign lane rather than a generic stall path.

conventions.name: branch-per-iteration-squash
conventions.semantics: Under PHASEKIT_SQUASH_TARGET, each squash commit on the target carries a trailer line '<marker><work-branch>@<short-sha>' naming the work-branch commit it was squashed from, and each merge-back commit on the work branch is titled 'chore(workflow): merge-back <target> after squash (phasekit v0.14.0)'. A supervisor's FULLY-MERGED predicate is tree equality: `git diff --quiet <target> <work-branch>` — a completed iteration whose final squash was refused is NOT resting. The target moves only through the loop's squash; any other movement fails the next squash closed (phase-blocked.json, blocker_kind branch-integrity).

conventions.name: verify-gate-read-only
conventions.marker: a verify gate is read-only over tracked files and writes nothing untracked
conventions.semantics: v0.14.10. The rule, verbatim: a verify gate is read-only over tracked files and writes nothing untracked; gate output belongs under an ignored path. The loop proves it rather than trusting it — `git status` before and after the gate command; the paths that appeared are the gate's footprint. A non-empty footprint is restored (tracked paths back to HEAD, untracked ones deleted) and the gate is RED even when its command exited 0, with gate_footprint / gate_footprint_rule / gate_footprint_recipe in artifacts/phase-verify-failed.json; the existing red-gate machinery (CONTINUE_PROMPT step 2, VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, the red verify memo — which carries the footprint so a replay is the same red) carries the fix to the next pass. No opt-in and no declaration surface exist. Dirt present before the gate is the session's staged work and its staged bytes are never touched; a gate that rewrites such a file in the worktree (a formatter with a write flag, a re-measured evidence file) is caught by the worktree column flipping across the gate — restored to the staged bytes, red. A kill inside the gate is settled at the next loop start from the record's gate_pending (see boundary-state.json); while a gate is pending the deadline watchdog's last-resort commit commits the index as it stands (no `git add -A`), so the gate's worktree writes never ride a wip. A supervisor reads the artifact as before: a phase-verify-failed.json carrying gate_footprint is a project whose gate must be fixed, never a landing to repair by hand; the dirty-rest shape this rule removes (xmeo iterations 50–58) cannot arise from the gate any more.

conventions.name: roadmap-entries
conventions.semantics: v0.15.0. An OPTIONAL `docs/ROADMAP.md`; absent (ENOENT) is a valid state and nothing in the loop, the gates, the container, CONTINUE_PROMPT.txt or docs/QUALITY_GATES.md reads, requires or mentions it. Only three things in the file mean anything: the first line beginning `Direction:` (up to 3 spaces of indent; the current theme, free text; empty means none), and checkbox entries `- [ ] R<n> <title> — <scope> (needs: R<m>, …)` / `- [x] …` (bullet `-`, `*` or `+`, up to 3 spaces of indent) under the level-2 headings `## Next`, `## Later` and `## Done` (case-insensitive, a trailing colon tolerated, up to 3 spaces of indent; a level-3+ heading keeps its section, any other level-1/2 heading ends it). An entry's BODY is the non-blank lines after it indented deeper than its bullet, stopping at a blank line, a heading, a fence or HTML-comment opener, a `Direction:` line or another R<n> entry; id-less checkboxes in the body are the entry's own sub-tasks — not entries, not warned. A body line that looks like roadmap structure is never read silently: a wrapped `(needs:` or a checkbox at ANY indent (tabs included) whose text starts with an R<n>-shaped token is warned and EXCLUDES the owning entry (and `done` refuses it) until the user unwraps or outdents it. Everything else is ignored: prose, other headings and what sits under them, fenced code blocks (CommonMark: a fence closes only on the same character at no shorter length with nothing after it; a backtick info string containing a backtick is inline code, not a fence), HTML comments, and indented code. A leading UTF-8 BOM is tolerated. Ids are `R<n>`, bridges `R<n>.<k>`, with no leading zeros, APPEND-ONLY: never renumbered, reused or deleted; to replace an entry keep its line and write the marker right after the id, EXACTLY, followed by the replacement id and a colon-space (`- [ ] R2 SUPERSEDED by R5: old title`) — a near miss (another case, no colon) is excluded and warned, never read as live; a `needs:` naming a superseded id is satisfied by the end of its supersession chain. `(needs: …)` must be the LAST thing on an unchecked entry's line and appear once. An entry is done when it is checked, wherever it sits. ELIGIBLE = under `## Next`, unchecked, not superseded, its id on exactly one entry line within the three sections (an R<n> checkbox under any other heading is ignored and warned, and does not count), every `needs:` done; `## Later` is never eligible. `scripts/phasekit-roadmap.py next` is the one reader: JSON {schema 1, file, absent, direction, eligible [{id, title, scope, needs}], blocked [{…, waiting_on}], exhausted, counts {next, later, done}, warnings [{line, message}]}. What it skips is reported, never silent: a checkbox with no valid id outside an entry's body, an id on more than one line (EVERY copy excluded), a misplaced or malformed `needs:`, a `needs:` naming an id not in the file, a near-miss or dangling supersession, a supersession cycle, a needs cycle (followed THROUGH supersession and reported once per group of mutually-waiting entries, every member named), an R<n> checkbox outside the three sections, and a fence or HTML comment that never closes (which would otherwise swallow the rest of the file). `done R<n> --iteration LABEL` is the one writer: it keeps the entry's line VERBATIM except that the mark flips to `x` and ` — iteration LABEL (YYYY-MM-DD)` is appended (trailing whitespace trimmed), moves the entry's body with it, and inserts it directly after the last existing `## Done` entry's body (or under the heading); it changes no other line except to add a missing final newline to the line before the insertion point, or to append a blank line and `## Done` at the end of the file when that section is absent. It holds an advisory lock on the file's directory across read-modify-write, writes atomically through a symlink to its target via a temp file named `.phasekit-roadmap-write-<8 chars>.tmp` (only that exact shape is ever swept after a killed writer), refuses a read-only file, and keeps CRLF and a BOM. LABEL is one line with no control or line-separator characters. Re-marking a done entry is a no-op. A supervisor moves entries only through it.

conventions.name: loop-commit-trailers
conventions.semantics:
v0.18.0. Every loop-authored commit ends in one trailer block (the Gerrit Change-Id shape: machine keys stable across rewording; subjects are for humans): `Phasekit-Iteration: ` (the supervisor's iteration label from artifacts/iteration-mode.json, a leading 'iteration' word stripped; absent in a standalone run), `Phasekit-Phase:

` (the phase the commit closes or, on a checkpoint, names — a leading 'phase' word stripped; absent when underivable), and `Phasekit-Kind: `, one of phase | completion | update | squash | merge-back | wrapup | wip | heal | claim (a deploy claim an unverified wip kept out, landed verify-gated at the next start). A squash keeps its `phasekit-squash: @` line first in the same block. A supervisor's intake commit carries `Phasekit-Iteration: ` and `Phasekit-Kind: intake`, which the loop reads as the iteration's base. Readers use `git log --format='%(trailers:key=Phasekit-Iteration,valueonly)'`, never the subject. A missing fact has no trailer (fork F5: its absence is honest, never a refusal).

conventions.name: commit-subject-prefix
conventions.semantics:
v0.18.0 (commitizen, not commitlint: generated, never linted or refused). The subject of an approval-class commit (phase, completion, and its squash) is `iteration phase

: ` (standalone: `phase

: `), N from the supervisor, P from the verdict, the prose from `suggested_commit_message` (else the record's summary) minus any facts prefix the session wrote (text before the first ': ' that starts with 'iteration' or 'phase' and a number). A session prefix that DISAGREES with the record is corrected and its prose replaced by the record's `iteration_label` or `summary` (a stale prefix means stale prose), printing `commit subject corrected: '' → '' (the record says so)`. When P cannot be derived the subject stays as written (a WARN when supervised) except that a disagreeing iteration is still corrected. v0.18.2 (row 1233): after the prefix the subject is the PLANNED phase title from docs/PHASES.md (a heading `Phase

` or `Meta Phase

` — a bare id only when it is not purely numeric — followed by a separator (— – - : or '. '), never a progress or status record; of those the shallowest level, then the last; status words and an over-long trailing parenthetical dropped, at most 100 characters); the session's prose (as corrected above) moves to the commit BODY. With no planned title the prose stays the subject and the loop prints `commit subject: docs/PHASES.md plans no title for phase

…`.

conventions.name: loop-owns-commits
conventions.semantics: v0.18.2 (queue row 1233, Aaron 2026-09-30). Under the loop (PHASEKIT_ARTIFACTS_DIR + PHASEKIT_ITER_MARKER in the environment) the PreToolUse command guard refuses a model's git commands that write this repository's history, refs or index — commit, commit-tree, add, rm, mv, reset, restore, checkout with arguments, switch, stash (except list/show), merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, am, pull, fetch, tag, branch write forms, update-ref, update-index, read-tree, worktree (except list), and the write forms of notes, replace, reflog, submodule, remote, symbolic-ref, bisect, sparse-checkout and apply — with ONE plain line (exit 2); read-only git is allowed; a write aimed at another repository is not refused; an interactive session is unaffected. Every session prompt states the rule. The loop's own git is unaffected. The safety net for what the guard cannot see: at every completion the loop checks the whole tree (boundary-state.json `unlanded`). v0.18.3 (Aaron 2026-09-30, the operator lane): under the loop the guard ALSO refuses any `git push` (from any repository — only the loop publishes); "under the loop" means both variables are NON-EMPTY — their paths need not exist, so a model deleting the /tmp marker or moving artifacts/ never turns the rule off. In an interactive session only the destructive list applies (see the hook's exit code 2): an ordinary push, tag or commit is allowed, and the shared settings' deny list names only the destructive push and tag forms.

conventions.name: planned-paths
conventions.semantics: v0.18.2 (queue row 1233). A phase MAY declare the paths it expects to change: one or more lines `Planned paths: <glob>, <glob> …` (commas or spaces; backticks optional; `Planned paths: none` declares the empty set) inside its docs/PHASES.md section (its heading to the next heading of the same or a higher level; not in a code fence). Globs are relative to the repository root: `*` stays in one path segment, `**` crosses segments, `?` is one character, `[…]` is a character class (`[!…]` negated), a trailing `/` or a glob-free name also covers everything under it. The phase's section is found by the same heading rule as the commit subject. Always planned: artifacts/**, docs/PHASES.md, docs/LEARNINGS*.md. At every approval-class landing the loop compares the phase's changed paths (the staged diff since the evidence file's `since`) with the declaration and records `plan_paths` in the landed record, the phase-close evidence file and boundary-state.json: {schema: 1, phase, source, declared, globs, status, changed_count, unplanned, unplanned_count, note?} — status `inside` (unplanned_count 0), `outside` (unplanned_count > 0; `unplanned` lists at most 200), `no-plan-declared` (declared false, unplanned_count null — never zero) or `underivable` (no phase id or no base); changed_count excludes the always-planned paths. One stderr line per landing names the result. Warn only: never a refusal.

conventions.name: deferral-ledger
conventions.semantics: v0.18.0 (the changesets shape). A verdict record describes THIS iteration only: `deferrals` lists the entries it opened, `closes` the keys it closed. At every approval-class landing the loop upserts the entries by key into artifacts/deferrals.json (the open set; an entry copied forward out of habit is 'unchanged', never new) and removes the closed keys; a COMPLETION record's committed `deferrals` is then the full open set, so every reader of the record reads what copy-forward produced. The ledger's first composition seeds it from the last committed completion record (the check: on that first landing its key set equals that record's). Keys follow approval-deferrals (explicit, else AC#n, else a slug); a keyless entry cannot enter the ledger.

conventions.name: phase-close-evidence
conventions.semantics: v0.18.0. What an iteration or a phase changed is answered by phasekit, never rebuilt from `git rev-list --grep=<subject>`: the model-facing `phasekit scope [--iteration N] [--phase P] [--json]` (base, HEAD, the phase commits by trailer, the changed paths with status — it may read git), and the evidence file every approval landing commits (artifacts, `iterations`), which a test reads as a golden from the tree (hermetic-tests).

conventions.name: hermetic-tests
conventions.semantics: v0.18.0. A test reads the current tree and declared fixtures, never git history (no git log / rev-list / show <rev>: / blame / diff <rev> from a test); a fact about the past is an evidence file. The rule is adopted, not enforced (enforcement would refuse, and refusing is a stall): after the gate the loop prints, once per session, `ADVISORY: N test files appear to read git history (…first 5…) … see docs/QUALITY_GATES.md "Hermetic tests"` — never a red gate, never a row.

conventions.name: declared-surface
conventions.semantics: v0.18.3 (queue row 1194, Aaron 2026-09-30). A test reads the project's own tree and phasekit's DECLARED surface — this file, whose `facts` section `phasekit facts --json` (scripts/phasekit-surface.py) prints — never a scaffold-owned file (`ownership: scaffold` in .scaffold/manifest.json: the vendored loop and scripts, the hooks, the scaffold docs); a fact a test needs that the surface lacks is a request to phasekit, not a parse. Adopted, not enforced (a refusal is a stall): the advisory `scaffold-reads` names offenders. After the gate the loop prints, once per session, `ADVISORY scaffold-reads: N test file(s) read scaffold-owned files (…first 5…) …` and writes artifacts/boundary-state.json `scaffold_reads` (and `scaffold_reads_at`, when; null = the scan failed) = [{"test": <tracked test file>, "paths": [<scaffold-owned paths it reads>]}] sorted by test ([] = scanned, none found; carried across pass starts; absent = never scanned); `phasekit check` prints the same advisory without changing its exit code; `phasekit scaffold-reads --json` prints {"advisory": "scaffold-reads", "scaffold_reads": […], "line": <the printed line or empty>}. A read = a tracked test CODE file (the hermetic advisory's test-path selection, .py/.ts/.js/.sh and kin, fixtures/ excluded) that reads a scaffold-owned path — the literal, or its pieces joined (`ROOT / "scripts" / "x.sh"`, `path.join(root, 'scripts', 'x.sh')`) — directly or through a variable assigned that path. v0.18.5: decided on the file's CODE, not its lines: the file is lexed (code, string literals, comments, JS regex literals, shell heredoc bodies), and a read is a call written in code (open/read_text/readFileSync/readFile/a read-, load-, parse- or extract-named helper; a capitalised name constructs a value and reads nothing) with the path as one whole literal (under a directory prefix at most) or joined literal pieces among ITS OWN arguments, nested calls included, never inside a list, map or tuple literal there; a member read on it (`.read_text()`, `.open()`); or a shell read (cat/grep/sed/awk/head/tail/source/`.`) at a command position in a shell test (inside a `$( … )` too, in double quotes or an unquoted heredoc), or as a command string handed to a call that runs commands. A callee counts when the word starts its name or a `_`/camelCase part (`already_installed`, `download` are not reads), and `open(…, "w")` writes. A path that is only data — a code sample inside a string, a comment, a forbidden-path list, an expected value — is not a read (xmeo-v3's guard test, which refuses scaffold reads, was flagged for the paths it plants). Residual, by design (a false positive files a fix row downstream): a path built at run time, a read inside `bash -c "…"` in a shell test, a command list assembled before the call that runs it, a helper whose name does not say it reads, a path passed through a second name, a path joined at run time (`[…].join('/')`) or looked up in a map, JSX/TSX text, and a JS regex literal right after `)` (lexed as a division) are not seen; a predicate whose name says it reads (`isScaffoldRead('…')`) is still counted. Reading contracts/interface.json or a vendored provider copy under vendor/contracts/ is the declared surface and never flagged; running a scaffold script is not reading it.

conventions.name: session-cost-lines
conventions.semantics: v0.18.0. Lines the loop prints to its stdout (the supervisor's session log) — the single source of the session-efficiency numbers; a supervisor never computes them a second time. (1) At arm: `deadline watchdog: armed — sentinel at T-<L>s, last-resort commit at T-<LR>s (span <S>s), take control at T-<Ty>s[ (build turn T-<Tb>s)]` — the lead in force; a supervisor arms no lead of its own. (2) `phasekit-cost: <one-line JSON>` {schema: 1, mode, bound_s, lead_s, take_control_s, lead_uncapped_s, lead_cap_s, at_cap, heavy, heavy_in_previous_4, p90_s: {g_full, g_fast, w, m, r, pass} (null = no sample; the lead then used a prior), samples: {measure: count}}. `heavy` = the full tier's measured P90 over 12.5% of the bound, or the uncapped lead over the cap (only once the full tier has a sample) — the fork-F4 fact; the supervisor's threshold is 2 of the last 5 sessions (heavy_in_previous_4 + this one). (3) `deadline watchdog: took control — …` when the watchdog ended a model turn at the take-control point (the watchdog's own log says `took control at T-<Ty>s`).

facts._about: v0.18.3 (queue row 1194, Aaron 2026-09-30). The facts phasekit DECLARES for downstream tests and supervisors: read these (this section, or `phasekit facts --json`, which prints it) instead of parsing phasekit's scaffold-owned files. `version` changes when a fact changes meaning; a fact is only ever added, or changed with a version bump and a release note. Every fact is proven against the loop's behaviour by tests/test_declared_surface.py (`proven_by` names the tests), so a reshape of phasekit's internals that keeps these facts true cannot break a consumer that reads them. A fact a consumer needs that is missing here is a request to phasekit (docs/QUALITY_GATES.md "Tests read the declared surface").

commit_surfaces.summary: Every way the loop creates a commit, and the gates each one runs before it. `gates` names every gate that must pass before the commit (a set; the order is internal): `verify` (the project's gate, scripts/phasekit-verify.sh or PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CMD, with the contracts gate), `security_pair` (refuses staged .claude/settings.json or .github/workflows/), `post_verify` (the post-verify commit gates, with `context`). A NEW commit path is a contract change: it is declared here or the phasekit suite is red.

surfaces.creates: the commit of a verdict artifact — phase-approval.json, phase-update.json, project-complete.json (and the loop's own completion commit)
the soft-stop wrap-up commit: `chore(workflow): session wrap-up — soft stop before session end`
the commit landing a deploy claim the last unverified commit kept out: `chore(workflow): land the deploy claim the last unverified commit kept out`
the deadline watchdog's / wrap-up fall-through's last-resort commit (`--no-verify`): `wip: last-resort deadline commit (phasekit deadline watchdog) — …`
surfaces.notes: UNVERIFIED on purpose (it preserves work seconds before a kill). It never carries ready-to-deploy.json or project-complete.json changes; and unless a verify gate is mid-run (then it commits the index as it stands, the gate's own staging) it also unstages phase-approval.json, docs/LEARNINGS*.md, .claude/settings.json and .github/workflows/ — so outside that window it never carries what post_verify or security_pair would have refused. The next start lands the work verify-gated.

surfaces.creates: untracking committed transient signal artifacts: `chore(workflow): untrack transient signal artifacts (phasekit v0.6.5 heal)`
surfaces.notes: removes index entries only; adds no content

surfaces.creates: branch-per-iteration: the squash of the work branch onto the target (git commit-tree)
surfaces.notes: the squash judges only a worktree equal to HEAD's tree; its verify gate is answered by the verify memo when one records a green verdict for exactly that tree, else it runs

surfaces.creates: branch-per-iteration: re-entering an existing work branch that lacks the target's tip, the loop merges the target in (git merge --no-edit; a conflict is aborted and blocks the project instead)
surfaces.notes: records trees both branches already carry; nothing the session wrote

surfaces.creates: branch-per-iteration: the merge of the target back into the work branch (git commit-tree)
surfaces.notes: records trees both branches already carry

returns.4: light mode (context iteration) only: escalate to a standard iteration, no commit

scope_warning.summary: A post-verify gate member: the staged paths whose `.scaffold/manifest.json` entry has `"ownership": "scaffold"` are scope hits. Hits are written to artifacts/scope-warning.json {scope_warning: true, files: [<sorted hits>], ts}. In context iteration under light mode the commit is NOT made (return 4, escalation); otherwise a warning is printed and the commit proceeds. No manifest, or no hit: nothing is written.

spec_change.summary: A post-verify gate member: when docs/SPEC.md is staged the loop records its numstat in artifacts/spec-change.json {spec_changed: true, added_lines, removed_lines, ts} and proceeds. Never a refusal.

learnings_credential_scan.summary: A post-verify gate member (since v0.4.7): every STAGED file whose path matches `staged_files_ere` is grepped (grep -E) with `ere`; any match REFUSES the commit (return 1, the line named on stderr, redacted in the repair turn's capture). `ere` is `patterns` joined with `|`. The same token patterns redact every capture the loop records.

learnings_size_advisory.summary: At loop start, when docs/LEARNINGS.md is at or over the threshold — whole KiB, bytes // 1024 >= PHASEKIT_LEARNINGS_WARN_KB (default 48) — the loop prints a curation note on stderr. Advisory only.

completion_record.summary: artifacts/project-complete.json across a loop run: at every iteration start the loop removes it (an untracked one is unstaged first) — EXCEPT this iteration's own committed completion while its landing is still in flight, whose committed bytes are kept (restored if the disk copy differs). A deletion already on disk is left. A completion the gate refused is CARRIED (kept on disk, unstaged, claiming nothing until re-written); a carried record nobody re-claimed is removed at session exit and at the next loop start. Between supervisor iterations nothing here changes: the supervisor's intake removes the record.
completion_record.kept_while_landing: this iteration's committed completion, while its landing is in flight

recovery_only_run.summary: MAX_ITERATIONS=0 runs the loop-start recovery (stranded verdicts landed verify-gated) and exits without a single model turn.
recovery_only_run.exit: 3 (the iteration limit reached) unless the recovery landed the project's completion (0), per exit_codes of scripts/run-until-done.sh

container.summary: What scripts/container-setup.sh gives the container. Secrets travel by NAME: `docker run -e NAME` with the value exported into docker's own environment — never on docker's command line, where every host account can read it (since v0.18.2). PHASEKIT_FORWARD_ENV names cross the same way; the reserved names are refused. PHASEKIT_ITERATION_MODE crosses only when set non-empty.

hermetic_tests.summary: The hermetic-tests advisory (conventions `hermetic-tests`): tracked files matching `test_path_ere` (minus node_modules/) that match `history_read_ere` (grep -E) are named.

scaffold_reads.summary: The `scaffold-reads` advisory (conventions `declared-surface`): the advisory id, the boundary-state.json field, and the one-line prefix it prints.

loop_lines.summary: Lines the loop prints that a supervisor may key on: each `prefix` starts the line, `stream` is where it goes: stdout, stderr, or a log file under artifacts/logs/ (the deadline watchdog runs in a background subshell whose output goes to its own log). The armed and cost lines are the `session-cost-lines` convention.

wrapup_sentinel_skip.prefix: === Wrap-up requested (sentinel present) — not starting iteration

verify_breaker.summary: The pre-commit verify breaker's phase-blocked.json `reason` when the gate failed its attempts.

scaffold_manifest.summary: .scaffold/manifest.json, written by the phasekit engine at every adopt/upgrade: its keys, the per-file keys, the ownership vocabulary and the normalization recipe `sha256` is taken over (`sha256_strict` is the raw bytes). The manifest never lists itself.

codes.0: finished cleanly: project completion committed, wrap-up sentinel honoured, deadline pacing wrapped up, or stranded work recovered with nothing left to do
codes.1: loop-owned failure: a required command (jq, git) is missing, or the session ended with NO verdict artifact and the loop cannot dispatch (the silence failure the Stop hook exists to prevent)
codes.2: stopped, external input required: phase-blocked.json present, a commit was blocked, or a light-mode run escalated
codes.3: MAX_ITERATIONS reached without project completion (light mode also writes light-escalation.json with trigger iteration_cap)

scripts/run-until-done.sh.passthrough: Any other code is the claude CLI's own exit, propagated verbatim after the PHASEKIT_ITER_RETRY budget is exhausted — including 124 from a supervisor-side timeout and 137 from SIGKILL. The loop assigns meaning only to 0/1/2/3. v0.18.0: the `verify` and `scope` subcommands (what `phasekit verify`/`phasekit scope` run) exit 0 green/answered, 1 red/unanswerable, 2 usage, 3 verify skipped (the tier's measured P90 is over 540 s) — they start no iteration. A turn the deadline watchdog ended at the take-control point (SIGTERM, claude exits 143) is not a CLI failure: no retry, and the run ends 0 after its verify-gated landing / wrap-up. v0.18.1: when the watchdog could not write its marker, a turn that started before its take-control instant and ended non-zero after it is read as taken (the log says `took control (inferred …`) — never a retry; and a turn the completion guard ended (the completion record was committed during it) is not a CLI failure either: no retry, and the loop lands it (`verify` exits 2 when the index is locked).

codes.1: usage error: no prompt-file argument, or the prompt file does not exist

scripts/run-phase.sh.passthrough: Otherwise the claude CLI's exit status, unmodified (pipefail); nothing is remapped.

codes.0: nothing declared, or every declared contract byte-matches the provider (also all status/provider/refresh success paths)
codes.2: malformed declaration or provider manifest (also missing pyyaml, and CLI usage errors)
codes.3: unobtainable: no provider mounted, or the provider does not offer a declared slug; refreshing cannot help
codes.4: drift: the vendored copy is missing or differs from the mounted one; fix is the named refresh command
codes.5: unverifiable: contracts.yaml exists but scripts/phasekit-contracts.py does not (scaffold predates v0.7.0). Emitted by the LOOP into phase-verify-failed.json, never by the checker itself; fix is phasekit upgrade

codes.0: success: `next` read docs/ROADMAP.md or found none (absent is exit 0 with absent true and exhausted true), `done` moved the entry or it was already done, `init` wrote the starter file
