codes.2: CLI usage error (argparse): unknown subcommand, a malformed R<n> id, a bad --date, or an empty/multi-line --iteration
codes.3: `done` only: the id is not in the roadmap, is superseded (the message names the replacement to mark instead), appears on more than one line, or its line does not parse
codes.4: `init` only: a roadmap already exists at the path; refused, never overwritten
codes.5: could not complete, and never means 'nothing is next': the --repo path is not a directory; the roadmap path is anything but a regular file or ENOENT (a dangling symlink — the file itself or any directory above it, since an unmounted place is not 'no roadmap' — a parent that is a file, a directory, a FIFO — which would otherwise hang the read); the file could not be read (permission, not UTF-8) or written (including a read-only file); `done` found no file at all; or an unexpected internal error (never a traceback exit 1). Exit 0 with exhausted true means the reader LOOKED: the repo is a directory and the roadmap path is either ENOENT or a regular file that was read

codes.0: success: `facts` printed the declared facts; `scaffold-reads` always exits 0 — an advisory, never a refusal (none found prints nothing, or `"scaffold_reads": []` with --json)
codes.1: `facts` only: no contracts/interface.json with a `facts` section here or in the phasekit install (a project on phasekit before v0.18.3)
codes.2: CLI usage error: no verb, or an unknown verb

codes.1: precondition/config failure: docker missing, PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_MOUNT unusable (not a directory, or no readable index.json), or an unknown command

scripts/container-setup.sh.passthrough: Otherwise docker build's or the in-container process's exit status verbatim — so run-until-done.sh's codes surface unchanged, as do docker's own conventions (125/126/127, 137 for docker kill).

codes.0: all executed checks passed (skipped checks count as neither)
codes.1: at least one check failed (aggregate; see the FAIL lines on stdout for which)

codes.0: success (check-version is informational and returns 0 even when behind)
codes.1: usage or I/O failure (missing target, unreadable manifest, non-canonical checkout for channel/self-update); v0.18.0 `verify`: the project's gate is RED; `scope`: nothing to answer (no base, no evidence and no commit for the phase)
codes.2: lock contention — another enrich-project.py holds the target's lock; v0.18.0 `verify`/`scope`: usage error, not run inside a phasekit project, or `verify --tier` naming the tier that does not run now; v0.18.1 `verify`: not run — git's index is locked (the message names the index.lock path, its age and what to do; nothing was staged or run, the lock is never removed by it)
codes.3: drift detected by the check verb (DRIFT / MISSING / TEMPLATE DRIFT); v0.18.0 `verify`: skipped — the tier's measured P90 is longer than a tool call may run (the commit gate runs it)

scripts/phasekit.sh.passthrough: The CLI execs scripts/enrich-project.py, so these are the engine's codes; a missing PHASEKIT_PYTHON interpreter surfaces as the shell's 126/127.

codes.0: allow the stop: hook inert (loop env absent), a fresh verdict artifact exists, the block budget is spent, or the counter is unwritable (cannot bound, so must not block)
codes.2: block the stop (Stop-hook contract): no verdict artifact newer than the iteration marker; bounded to PHASEKIT_STOP_BLOCK_LIMIT blocks per iteration

codes.0: nothing refused — including an empty payload; a parse the hook cannot complete falls back to a narrow regex over the command text (which may refuse), and any other internal failure allows (a hook never wedges a session)
codes.2: deny the tool call (PreToolUse hook contract): a DESTRUCTIVE command in any session (v0.18.3: git reset --hard; git clean -f with -d; a force or ref-deleting push — --force, -f, --force-with-lease, --delete/-d, --mirror, --prune, a +ref or :ref refspec; git tag -d/-f and git update-ref on refs/tags/; sudo; shred; a recursive rm of the repository's root, a directory above it, or its .git — an ordinary git push or git tag is NOT destructive and an interactive session may run it), or, under the loop, any git push, or a git command that writes this repository's history, refs or index (v0.18.2, the loop-owns-commits convention); ONE line on stderr

codes.0: always — contractually fail-open; internal python failures are swallowed and output is capped at 2048 bytes
success (for --upgrade: applied, gated green or skipped, and committed — or nothing to do; with no git identity, applied and gated but left uncommitted, a note naming it)
codes.1: error or bad input: no target, no manifest, an unusable PHASEKIT_UPGRADE_VERIFY value, a declined confirmation, a failed install (the upgrade's writes are restored)
codes.2: another process holds the target's lock, or --interactive combined with --yes
codes.3: --upgrade: unresolved refusals, nothing written; --check: drift, template-source drift, or an interrupted upgrade still pending
codes.4: --upgrade: no green verdict from the project's gate (red, timed out, wrote into the tree, or could not run here); every file restored, nothing committed
codes.5: --upgrade: applied and verified but NOT committed (staging or the commit failed, e.g. a stale .git/index.lock or a refusing pre-commit hook); the next --upgrade commits it
codes.130: --upgrade: interrupted by SIGINT/SIGTERM; before the verdict, every file the upgrade wrote is restored and nothing committed; after a green gate, the upgrade stays pending and the next --upgrade commits it

conventions.124: reserved for 'killed by an outer timeout wrapper'. No phasekit script ever exits 124 deliberately, so a supervisor may treat it as its own timeout reflected back.
conventions.137: SIGKILL (e.g. docker kill by a supervisor on hard deadline), propagated verbatim.
conventions.note: A wrapper distinguishing 'loop verdict' from 'child failure' relies on run-until-done.sh owning exactly 0/1/2/3 and everything else being passthrough.
